subject: mathematics
question_text: If A − B = 3π/4, show that (1 − tan A)(1 + tan B) = 2.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 31(i), book p.88. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1 + 1 gives one mark to turning the given difference into tan(A − B) = −1 and one to the expansion, where the group tan A − tan B has to be spotted before the substitution can be made. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A prints ten very short answers of 2 marks each and the student writes all ten, under the 2026-27 pattern; Trigonometric Ratios and Transformations supplies two of those ten slots. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would show this — name the value you get from the given condition, and where you use it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write tan(A − B) = −1
steps.margin_note: First mark. tan(3π/4) = −1. The expression asks for tan A and tan B, so both must exist: neither A nor B is an odd multiple of π/2.
steps.memory_tip: tan(3π/4) = −1. That single number is the whole point of the given condition.
lines: For tan A and tan B to exist, neither A
nor B is an odd multiple of π/2.
∴ (tan A − tan B)/(1 + tan A tan B) = −1
⇒ tan A − tan B = −1 − tan A tan B

recall.must_convey: That tan(A − B) = tan(3π/4) = −1 is written and expanded, giving tan A − tan B = −1 − tan A tan B.
accept: take tan on both sides and tan of three pi by four is minus one
expand tan A minus B and cross multiply
tan A minus tan B equals minus one minus tan A tan B
three pi by four ki tan minus one, adi expand cheyyali
use the tan A minus B formula

steps.why: 3π/4 is the only angle the question gives, and its tangent is −1. Turning the condition into that one number, and then clearing the denominator, is the whole first half of the proof.
common_mistakes: Using the tan(A + B) formula instead of tan(A − B).

steps.label: Expand the product and substitute
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Expand the bracket first — the group tan A − tan B appears, and step 1 replaces it. The two tan A tan B terms then cancel.
steps.memory_tip: Expand the bracket first. The group tan A − tan B shows up, and the condition replaces it.
lines: = 1 + tan B − tan A − tan A tan B
= 1 − (tan A − tan B) − tan A tan B
= 1 − (−1 − tan A tan B) − tan A tan B
= 1 + 1 + tan A tan B − tan A tan B

recall.must_convey: That the bracket is expanded, tan A − tan B is replaced using step 1, and the tan A tan B terms cancel to leave 2.
accept: expand the bracket and the group tan A minus tan B appears
substitute minus one minus tan A tan B for tan A minus tan B
the tan A tan B terms cancel and two is left
bracket expand cheste tan A minus tan B group vasthundi
reject: tan of three pi by four is minus one

steps.why: Expanding first is what makes the substitution possible: the expansion contains the group tan A − tan B, which is exactly what the condition supplies. Substituting it makes the two tan A tan B terms cancel and leaves a pure number.
common_mistakes: Expanding as 1 + tan A − tan B − tan A tan B.
Replacing tan A − tan B by −1 alone and dropping the tan A tan B term.
